name: Paddy Pallin Landscape Restoration Grants
summary: Multi-year grants for small community environment groups doing long-term bush regeneration in NSW and the ACT: weed control, riparian and creek-line restoration, habitat structures, monitoring tied to on-ground works and local-provenance seed work.

geography.label: New South Wales and the ACT

amount.note: No minimum; projects run three years or more, each year's funding after a satisfactory progress report

reporting: Recipients report annually, in writing and by video, on progress against their deliverables; the Foundation also inspects sites.

steps: Written application by email, covering the guide's eight sections
Grants committee review, with possible questions or a site visit

eligibility.rule: Community organisation devises and leads the project
Public conservation land or private land with a registered conservation agreement, including mixed tenure
Younger members hold real field leadership or governance roles
Project goes beyond research as an end in itself
Project excludes advocacy campaigns and lobbying

deadline.quote: Applications open on 20 October 2026 and close on 20 January 2027.

applicant_types.quote: We fund non-government organisations rather than individuals.

geography.quote: Your site must be in New South Wales or the Australian Capital Territory, on public land held for conservation.

access.quote: If you would like to discuss a project before applying, contact us.

window.quote: Applications open on 20 October 2026 and close on 20 January 2027.

amount.quote: Grants are up to $30,000, and there is no minimum.

co_finance_required.quote: We encourage applicants to secure funding from additional sources, and we assess such applications favourably.

consortium_required.quote: If you are applying with partner organisations, a council, National Parks and Wildlife Service or a Landcare group, who does what and who is accountable for the funded work.

reporting.quote: Recipients report annually, demonstrating progress against the deliverables they committed to. Reporting is written and video.

effort.quote: Download the program guide and work through the eight sections it sets out.

Send your application, or any questions about the program, to the Foundation by email. If you are unsure whether your project fits, contact us before applying. info@paddypallinfoundation.org.au APPLICATIONS OPEN 20 October 2026 APPLICATIONS CLOSE 20 January 2027
Our grants committee reads every application, and we may come back with questions or arrange a site visit before deciding.

eligibility.quote: The project itself must be devised and led by the community organisation.

Your site must be in New South Wales or the Australian Capital Territory, on public land held for conservation. Private land is eligible where a conservation agreement, such as a Voluntary Conservation Agreement, is registered over it. Mixed and joint tenure qualify on the same basis.

We need to see younger members helping steer the groups we fund. That means younger people leading work parties and field programs, and holding board positions, office-holder roles and other positions of genuine responsibility.
The exclusion applies to funding research as an end in itself, not to evidence-based practice:
The following fall outside this program: Advocacy campaigns and lobbying

after_award.quote: Recipients report annually, demonstrating progress against the deliverables they committed to.
The Foundation also conducts on-ground inspections.

documents.quote: Attach photographs of the site as it currently stands, and a short video walking through it if you can.
